 : JUDGMENT :

The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996 and requested this Court to set aside the Arbitral Award dated 17.03.2020 passed in case No.LAQ/ARB/NH- 7/CR/12/2013-14 pertaining to Sy.No.66 by respondent No.2 A.P. No.7/2021 .2.
In the petition it is stated that National Highways Authority of India was constituted by an Act of the Parliament, "the National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988" .

entities.text: National Highways Authority of India Act, 1988
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is responsible for the development, maintenance and management of National Highways entrusted to it and for matters connected thereto.

.3. It is stated that the Central Government for the purpose of widening / upgradation maintenance,
management and operation of NH-7 on the stretch of land from kms. 526.50 to kms. 535 & Kms.
539 to Kms 556 of Hyderabad - Bengaluru Section issued preliminary notification dated 05.12.2002 under Section 3-A(1) of the National Highways Act, 1956 in-respect of acquisition of lands situated at Kadiganahalli village, Bengaluru North Taluka.
The preliminary notification was published on 25.12.2002.

The final notification was published in the official Gazette on 22.07.2003.
.4.

It is stated that under the said notification for the 1st stage of acquisition non-agricultural lands in Sy.No. 66 to an extent of 2043.69 sq. feet, situated at A.P. No.7/2021 the said village belonging to the respondent No. 1 were also acquired.
.5.
It is stated that the respondent No.3 vide award dated 08.03.2004 determined the market value of NA lands at Rs.45/- per sq. feet.
The respondent No. 3 observed that the average of the sale statistics of NA lands was Rs. 46/- per sq. feet and the guidance value was Rs. 45/- per sq. feet.

Since both the average of the sales statistics as well as the guidance value were on almost the same, the respondent No. 3 examined the physical characteristics of the acquired lands, relied upon the guidance value and determined the market value of NA lands at Rs. 45/- per sq. feet.
.6.
It is stated that a sum of Rs.91,966/- was disbursed as compensation to the respondent No.1 towards the subject lands.
Being dissatisfied with the amount awarded by the respondent No.3 the respondent No.1 belatedly approached the respondent No.2 under Section 3-G (5) of the NH Act.

on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11956999/
2 is stated that the petitioner entered appearance and filed its A.P. No.7/2021 statement of objections with documents in support of his defence.
The respondent No.2 passed an arbitral award and redetermined the market value at Rs.125/- per sq. feet for the subject lands acquired from respondent No.1.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner has preferred this petition on the following grounds:
(a) The impugned Arbitral Award passed by the respondent No.2 is perverse, patently illegal;
(b) The 1st stage acquisition award was passed by the respondent No. 3 on approached the respondent No. 2 seeking enhancement of compensation on 08.01.2013 and the respondent No. 2 has completely failed to note that the claims of respondent No. 1 were barred by time.
(c) The respondent No. 2 has erroneously stated the nature of lands as dry instead of NA which indicates the non-application of mind to the facts of the case.
A.P. No.7/2021 (d) The respondent No. 2 has not complied with the provision of Section 28 of the A & C Act, while passing the impugned award and therefore, it is patently illegal and requires to be set aside.
(e) The respondent No. 2 has not made any attempt to investigate the market value of the subject lands as on the date of publication of preliminary notification.

(f) For the purpose of enhancement of compensation the respondent No. 2 has relied upon the guidance value for the year 2005-06 dated 07.10.2005 which provides that the guidance value of NA lands was at has relied upon the same and awarded compensation at Rs. 125/- per sq. feet.
(g) the respondent No. 2 has relied upon a notification, which came into effect after the publication of preliminary notification, the impugned award is opposed to Section 3- G(7)(a) of the NH Act.
A.P. No.7/2021 (h) The respondent No. 2 has also failed to follow the procedure laid down in Section 24 of the A & C Act.

(i) The respondent No. 2 has given the benefit of enhancement to the respondent No. 1 without production by the respondent No. 1 of any records or evidence in support of such enhancement which is completely arbitrary.
(j) The impugned Arbitral Award is not a speaking order and liable to be set aside.

A.P./7/2021 on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11956999/
3

(k) The respondent No. 2 has neither complied with the procedure provided under Section 24 nor decided the dispute in accordance with Section 28(1)(a) and at the same time has failed to comply with Section 31(3) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, thus rendering the impugned arbitral award opposed to settled position of law on all the three counts.
The impugned Arbitral Award was passed on 17.03.2020.
The certified copy of the impugned arbitral award was received by the petitioner on 15.12.2020.
Thereafter, the petitioner took necessary steps through its counsel to apply and obtain the certified copy of the impugned arbitral award.

The petition is being filed in accordance with the notification issued by the Hon'ble High Court extending the closure of this Court till 31.01.2021 for the purpose of Section 4 of the Limitation Act, 1963.
Hence, the petition is in time.
.8. The respondent No.1 has filed Cross objections stating that the land in question is converted land for non-agricultural purpose.
The Arbitrator has not considered the value of the acquired land and awarded meager amount, which is not enough to acquire alternative land.
It is stated that the Arbitrator has failed to appreciate with respect to increase of land value.
Further failed to appreciate the acquired land was capable of being used as commercial purpose.

The Court below has relied upon land acquisition order A.P. No.7/2021 based on notification numbered CVC 19/2010 dated 21.09.2011 and has fixed the rate at Rs. 1500/- per sq. feet without considering the ground reality and the commercial value, which is bad in law.
The value of the land should have been assessed at least Rs. 5,000/- per sq. feet, which is just and proper assessment under Section 3G(2) of National Highways Authority Act.
Solatium has not been awarded, further additional market value under the prevailing circumstances has not considered while passing award.

.9. The petitioner has filed objections to the cross objections filed by the respondent No. 2 stating that the cross objection filed by the respondent No. 1 seeking setting aside of the Arbitral Award dated 17.03.2020 along with a direction to reconsider the matter at prevailing market value is not maintainable.

It is stated that if the respondent No. 1 is aggrieved by the Arbitral Award he has to prefer an independent application under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act within the time period as stipulated under Section A.P. No.7/2021 34(3) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act and he cannot seek for any relief in an application which is filed by the petitioner.

.10. It is stated that the respondent No. 1 has further sought for a direction to reconsider the matter as per prevailing market value which indicates that he has sought for remand of the matter back to the respondent No. 2 which is impermissible in the eyes of law.

It is stated that no independent application is preferred by the respondent No. 1 and even assuming for the sake of arguments that the cross objection is maintainable, still the relief of remand is beyond the scope of Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

The plain reading of Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act clearly establish that courts have no powers under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act either to remand or to remit the matter back to the arbitral tribunal once the arbitral award is set aside.

It is stated that the respondent No. 1 also cannot seek any enhancement A.P. No.7/2021 since the scope of interference under Section 34(2) of Arbitration and Conciliation Act is very limited assuming that the cross objection is maintainable.

A.P./7/2021 on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11956999/
4 .11.

It is stated that the Civil Court while deciding an application under Section 34 cannot sit in a Court of Appeal and re-appreciate the evidence led before the arbitrator especially when there is no independent challenge to the Arbitral Award.
.12.
It is stated that the date of preliminary notification in case of Kadiganahalli village was 05.12.2002.

There is absolutely no scope of considering the prevailing market value or increasing market value since the market value has to be strictly determined as on the date of publication of preliminary notification as provided under Section 3-G(7)(a) of the NH Act.

If the respondent No. 1 was aggrieved by the non-awarding of the relief/s as stated by him, he had the liberty to approach this Court in accordance with sub-section (2) and (3) of Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
It is stated that the cross objection is misconceived A.P. No.7/2021 and outside the scope of Section 34(2) of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
Hence, prayed to reject the cross objection.
.13. Heard the arguments.
Perused the written arguments filed by both sides.

.14. The following points that would arise for my consideration are:
(1) Whether petitioner in A.P. No.7/2021 has made out sufficient grounds under Section 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act to set aside the arbitral award dated 17.03.2020 passed by respondent No. 2?
(2) Whether the cross objection filed by the respondent No.1 can be considered?
(3) What order or award?

.15. My findings on the above points are:
Point No.1 : In the affirmative Point No.2 : In the negative Point No.3 : As per final order, for the following:
A.P. No.7/2021 REASONS .16.

POINT No.1: The respondent No. 3 has acquired NA land in Sy.No. 66 to an extent of 2043.69 sq. meters, situated at Kadiganahalli village, Bengaluru North Taluka belonging to the respondent No.1 for the purpose of widening of NH-7.
The preliminary notification was issued on 05.12.2002.
The respondent No. 3 passed the award on 08.03.2004 fixing market value at Rs. 45/- per sq. feet.
The respondent No. 1 dissatisfied with the award amount, approached the respondent No. 2 under Section 3-G(5) of the Act.
The respondent No. 2 redetermined the market value at Rs. 125/- per sq. feet.

Being aggrieved by the said award, the petitioner has preferred this petition under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
.17.
Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 provide the circumstances under which an award can be set aside by a Civil Court.
(2) It is in conflict with contravention with the fundamental policy of Indian Law or iii) It is in conflict with most basic notion of morality or justice.
A.P. No.7/2021 Explanation 2.
The test as to whether there is contravention with the fundamental policy of Indian law shall not entail a review on the merits of the dispute.

2A It may also be set aside if the Court finds the award is vitiated by patent illegality appearing on the face of award provided that an award shall not be set aside merely on the ground of an erroneous application of law or by re appreciation of evidence.

.18 . In Kwality Manufacturing Corporation Vs. Central Whorehouse Corporation (2009) 5 Sec.142, it has been held that:
"From a catena of other judgments of this Court, it is clear that for the objector /
appellant in order to succeed in their challenge against an arbitral award, they must show that the award of the Arbitrator suffered from perversity or an error of law or that the Arbitrator has otherwise misconducted himself.

entities.text: Kwality Manufacturing Corporation Vs. Central Whorehouse Corporation (2009) 5 Sec.142
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Merely showing that there is another reasonable interpretation or possible view on the basis of the material on the record is insufficient to allow for the interference by the Court."

Bearing in mind the above section and decision, now it has to be seen whether the impugned award suffers from any patent error, illegality as envisaged above.
A.P./7/2021 on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11956999/
6 .19.
The petitioner has stated that the award was passed by the respondent No.3 - L.A.O. on 08.03.2004.
The respondent No. 1 approached the respondent No. 2 seeking enhancement of compensation on 08.01.2013 after a lapse of more than 8 years from the date of passing of the award.
It is contended that the respondent No. 2 had failed to note the claim of respondent No. 1 was barred by time.

.20. In support of his contention, the petitioner counsel has relied upon the decision reported in (2016) 14 SCC 761 (State of Gujarath Vs. Kothari and Associates), wherein it has been held that:
" A. Limitation Act, 1963 - S. e - Issue of limitation - Duty of trial Court to consider, if said issue is not raised by parties concerned- Failure of trial Court to consider the issue in such a case - Effect of - Right to raise the issue in appeal. -
A.P. No.7/2021 Held, it is incumbent upon Trial Court to consider the issue of limitation on its own initiative even if that issue is not raised by parties concerned- Where the issue of limitation was not raised during trial by appellant State and also the trial Court failed to consider that issue on its own initiative, held, the said issue could be raised in appeal including any successive appeal."

entities.text: (2016) 14 SCC 761 (State of Gujarath Vs. Kothari and Associates)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The above decision applies to the case on hand.
.21. The preliminary notification in the present case was issued on 25.12.2002.
The award has been passed on 08.03.2004.
The compensation has been received by the respondent No.1 on 21.11.2012.
The application before the Arbitrator has been filed on 08.01.2013.

In-spite of taking specific contention with regard to limitation by the petitioner, the respondent No. 1 did not give any explanation with regard to delay in approaching the respondent No. 2 Arbitrator.

.22. As per Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act which reads as under:
"3G(5) - If the amount determined by the competent authority under Sub Section (1)
or Sub Section (2) is not acceptable to either of the parties, the A.P. No.7/2021 amount shall, on an application by either of the parties, be determined by the Arbitrator to be appointed by the Central Government."
.23.

In W.A. No. 31066/2012 & 31094-96/2012 (T. Yunis Vs. National Highways Authority of India and others), wherein our Hon'ble High Court has held that:
"No period of limitation has been stipulated to seek a reference under Section 3G(5)
of the National Highways Act.

entities.text: W.A. No. 31066/2012 & 31094-96/2012 (T. Yunis Vs. National Highways Authority of India and others)
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: In such circumstances, the only provision available to the parties is to invoke Article 137 of the Limitation Act, which provides three years from the date on which right to apply accrues".
The said decision applies to the case on hand.
As per the said decision within a period of 3 years from the date of passing of award right to file application before the Arbitrator arises.
The award has been passed on 08.03.2004.

The respondent No.1 ought to have filed the application before the A.P./7/2021 on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11956999/
7 Arbitrator on or before 08.03.2007.

As the application is filed on 08.01.2013 before the Arbitrator,
application was barred by limitation.
The Arbitrator has stated that the LAO has informed that the application can be filed within 3 years from the date of receipt of compensation and so the application is in time.
In this regard no document is available in the arbitral record.
The arbitrator could not have relied upon document without bringing to the notice of the parties.
The compensation amount is received by the respondent No.1 on 21.11.2012, even though the award has been passed on 08.03.2004.
The claimant has not explained the delay in filing the application.
The application filed before the Arbitrator is beyond 3 years and so the proceedings before the Arbitrator was barred by limitation.
.25. The petitioner has contended that Arbitrator has relied upon the guidance value for year 2005-06 published on 07.10.2005.
Preliminary notification in the present case was issued on 05.12.2002.

The petitioner has contended that the respondent No. 2 has relied upon the notification, which came to effect after A.P. No.7/2021 publication of preliminary notification, the impugned award is opposed to Section 3-G(7)(a) of the NH Act.
.26.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Oil & Natural Gas Corp. Ltd., Vs. SAW Pipes Ltd. (AIR 2003 SC 2629) has held that:
 "if the award is contrary to the  Substantive provisions of law or the provisions of the Act or against the terms of the contract, it would be patently illegal, which could be interfered under Section 34".

entities.text: Oil & Natural Gas Corp. Ltd., Vs. SAW Pipes Ltd. (AIR 2003 SC 2629)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The above decision applies to the case on hand.
The Arbitrator relying upon the guidelines value dated 07.10.2005 has enhanced the market value from Rs. 45/- per sq. feet to 125/- per sq. feet without assigning any reason.
Even if the Arbitrator had relied upon the said notification, he ought to have deescalated the value to the date of preliminary notification.
This he has not done so.
He has not complied with the statutory provisions of 3G (7)(a) of National Highways Authority Act.
Therefore, the award is patently illegal.
The Arbitrator has relied upon guidelines value 07.10.2005.
This document is not valid record received from the Arbitrator as none of the parties have produced and this is evident from the record of the Arbitrator.
Section 24(3) of the Act provides provision regarding hearing and written proceedings.

It reads thus:
"All statements, documents or other information supplied to, or applications made to the aribral tribunal by one party shall be communicated to the other party, and any expert report or evidentiary document on which the arbital tribunal may rely in making its decision shall be communicated to the parties".
.28.

As an Arbitrator has relied on the estimated guidelines value of immovable properties and buildings dated 07.10.2005 without bringing to the knowledge of the parties and thereby has failed A.P./7/2021 on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11956999/
8 to follow the procedure under Section 24 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
So the award has to be set aside on the ground of patent illegality.

The petitioner has contended that the respondent No.2 has not assigned any reasons for re- determining the compensation; that he has not assigned any reasons for enhancing the compensation or for relying upon notification dated 07.10.2005.
.30.

Section 3(G) of the National High Ways Act, mandatorily provides that, the competent authority or the Arbitrator to take into consideration the factors mentioned in Sub clause (a) to (d) while determining the market value of the compensation payable in-respect of the acquired lands.
But neither the award nor the order sheet shows any materials on record as to how he had followed the said provision.

.31. In Som Dutt Builders Ltd Vs. State of Kerala (2010)2 AWC (supp) 1390 SC) has held that:
"Reasons must be indicated in the award as that would reflect thought process leading to a particular conclusion.

entities.text: Som Dutt Builders Ltd Vs. State of Kerala (2010)2 AWC (supp) 1390 SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To satisfy the requirement of Section 31(3), the reasons must be stated by the Arbitral Tribunal upon which the award is based; want of reasons would make such award legally flawed."

On perusal of the records and the award of the Arbitrator it is seen that the respondent No.2 has neither complied with the procedure provided under Section 24 nor decided the dispute in accordance with Section 28(1)(a) and at the same time has failed to comply with Section 31(3) of the A & C Act, thus rendering the impugned Arbitral Award opposed to settled position of law.

.33. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Oil & Natural Gas Corp. Ltd. Vs. SAW Piles Ltd., (AIR 2003 SC 2629) has held that:
"if the award is patently against the statutory provisions of Substantive law which is in force in India or is passed without giving an opportunity of hearing to the parties as provided under Section 24 or without giving any reason in a case where parties have not agreed that no reasons are to be recorded

entities.text: Oil & Natural Gas Corp. Ltd. Vs. SAW Piles Ltd., (AIR 2003 SC 2629)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , it would be against the statutory provisions.
In all such cases, the award is required to be set aside on the ground of 'patent illegality'
The above decision is applies to the case in hand.
In view of the above discussion, I answer point No.1 in the affirmative.
Point No.2:
The respondent No. 1 has filed the Cross-objection on 06.01.2022 and has contended that the land in question is converted land for non- agricultural purpose.
The Arbitrator has not considered the value of the acquired land and awarded meager amount.
He failed to appreciate the acquired land was capable of being used for commercial purpose.

The value of the land ought to have A.P./7/2021 on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11956999/
9 been assessed at Rs.
5,000/- per sq. feet.

It is stated that the solatium has not been awarded, further additional market value under the prevailing circumstances has not considered while passing award and so has requested this Court to set aside the arbitral award and to direct to reconsider at the prevailing value.

As per Section 34(1) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act states that:
"34. Application for setting aside Arbitral Award - (1) Recourse to a Court against an Arbitral Award may be made only by an application for setting aside such award in accordance with Sub-section (2) and Sub-section (3)."
A.P. No.7/2021
From the above provisions, it is clear that Arbitral Award can be challenged only by an application under Sub Section (2) and there is no other alternative to the challenge.
.35. The respondent No. 1 has relied upon the decision of the High Court of Kerala reported in LA Appeal No. 953/2005 and C.O. No.125/2005, where the Hon'ble Court had dismissed the appeals.
The Cross Objections are upheld and the market value of the land acquired from the Cross Objections is re
-fixed at Rs. 9,000/- per cent.
Relying upon the said judgment the counsel for respondent No.1 has argued that Cross Objection is maintainable.
The said Cross Objection is filed in Appeal before the Hon'ble High Court.
The present petition under Section 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act is re-course against arbitral award.
It is not an appeal.
The provision of appeal is under Section 37 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
So, the Cross objection filed by the respondent No. 1 is not maintainable.

In ILR 2016 Karnataka 4136 (Bhaskar Industrial Development Ltd., Vs. South Western Railway), wherein it has been held that:
"A plain reading of Section 34 of the Act extracted above will show that parliament has not conferred any power of remand to the Court to remit the matter to the arbitral tribunal except to adjourn the proceedings as provided under Sub section (4)
of Section 34 of the Act.

entities.text: ILR 2016 Karnataka 4136 (Bhaskar Industrial Development Ltd., Vs. South Western Railway)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The object of Sub- section (4) of Section 34 is to give an opportunity to the arbitral tribunal to resume the arbitral proceedings or to enable it to take such other action which will eliminate the grounds for setting aside the arbitral award.

This provision cannot be invoked, once the arbitral award is set aside".
.37.

In 2018 (11) SCC 328 (Kinnari Mullick and another Vs. Ghansyham Das Damani), the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has confirmed the proposition laid down in Bhaskar Industrial Development Lits Vs. Southern Railway, wherein it has been held that:
A.P. No.7/2021 "remitting the matter back to the Arbitrator would constitute an error and that the Parliament has not conferred any power of remand under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996."

10 .38.

entities.text: 2018 (11) SCC 328 (Kinnari Mullick and another Vs. Ghansyham Das Damani)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Bhaskar Industrial Development Lits Vs. Southern Railway
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In ILR 2010 Karnataka 3711 ( Sri. H.M. Shankaramurthy Vs. National Highways Authority of India and others) , wherein it has been held that:
"... a provision for setting aside an award contending that the award is not sustainable in law on any one of the grounds as indicated above can never be construed as a provision enabling the land owner seeking for enhancement of the compensation amount as determined by the Arbitrator."

entities.text: ILR 2010 Karnataka 3711 ( Sri. H.M. Shankaramurthy Vs. National Highways Authority of India and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
.39. In 2017 (4) Karnataka L.J. 27/14 (NHAI Vs. Mahadevi and others), wherein it has been held that:
"We are satisfied that in view of the settled legal position, which is delineated below,
the learned Court below has grossly erred in setting aside the arbitral award and has further compounded the said error by substituting its own valuation and compensation amount which was simply not permitted within the scope of Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996".
A.P. No.7/2021 .40.

entities.text: 2017 (4) Karnataka L.J. 27/14 (NHAI Vs. Mahadevi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondent No. 1 has contended that the arbitrator has failed to appreciate the acquired land was capable of being used as commercial purpose and value of the land should have been assessed at Rs. 5,000/- per sq. feet.
To substantiate the same, the respondent No. 1 has not placed any documents before the Arbitrator.
So, the contention of respondent No. 1 cannot be accepted.
.41. In view of the above decisions, the reliefs sought by the respondent No. 1 to set aside the award and to direct the Arbitrator to re-consider the matter cannot be granted.

For the above discussion,
point No. 2 is answered in the negative.
.42. Point No.3:

In view of the aforesaid finding on point No.1 I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER A.P. No.7/2021 is allowed.

The impugned award passed by the respondent No.2 in so far as pertaining to case No.LAQ/ARB/NH- A.P. No.7/2021 7/CR/12/2013-14 pertaining to Sy.No.66 acquired to an extent of 2043.69 sq. feet is set aside.
The Cross-objection filed by respondent No. 1 is dismissed.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The respondent No.2 passed an arbitral award and redetermined the market value at Rs.125/- per sq. feet for the subject lands acquired from respondent No.1.
Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner has preferred this petition on the following grounds:
(a) The impugned Arbitral Award passed by the respondent No.2 is perverse, patently illegal;
(b) The 1st stage acquisition award was passed by the respondent No. 3 on approached the respondent No. 2 seeking enhancement of compensation on 08.01.2013 and the respondent No. 2 has completely failed to note that the claims of respondent No. 1 were barred by time.
(c) The respondent No. 2 has erroneously stated the nature of lands as dry instead of NA which indicates the non-application of mind to the facts of the case.
A.P. No.7/2021 (d) The respondent No. 2 has not complied with the provision of Section 28 of the A & C Act, while passing the impugned award and therefore, it is patently illegal and requires to be set aside.
(e) The respondent No. 2 has not made any attempt to investigate the market value of the subject lands as on the date of publication of preliminary notification.
(k) The respondent No. 2 has neither complied with the procedure provided under Section 24 nor decided the dispute in accordance with Section 28(1)(a) and at the same time has failed to comply with Section 31(3) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, thus rendering the impugned arbitral award opposed to settled position of law on all the three counts.
The respondent No. 1 dissatisfied with the award amount, approached the respondent No. 2 under Section 3-G(5) of the Act.
